newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil telecom law faces panel vote Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil telecom law faces panel vote Tuesday.

text.p: A bill laying down the rules for the privatization of Brazil's telecommunications industry might be put to a vote in a panel in the lower house of Congress on Tuesday, a congressional official said.
A panel studying the General Telecommunications Law was due to meet at 1400 local/1700 GMT and might vote on the bill, the official said.
If approved the bill advances to the floor of the Chamber of Deputies. It also has to pass through the Senate.
The bill would not limit foreign capital taking part in Brazilian telecommunications companies but would give the Brazilian president powers to restrict foreign investors on a case-by-case basis.
The legislation would also set up a new regulator to oversee the sector.

Under the legislative proposal, a regulator called the National Telecommunications Agency (Antel) would be given powers to prevent investors or groups of investors from dominating the industry. It would also have its own budget to ensure autonomy.
